claims.text: Standard LPBF of high-entropy-alloy powder commonly produces residual stresses.
Standard LPBF of high-entropy-alloy powder commonly produces porosity.
Standard LPBF of high-entropy-alloy powder commonly produces dimensional inaccuracies.
Preheating the build platform to approximately 200 °C decreases thermal gradients between the build plate and melt pool.
Decreasing thermal gradients reduces internal stresses during LPBF.
Decreasing thermal gradients reduces component distortion during LPBF.
Real-time dynamic laser-power modulation based on melt-pool monitoring improves control of melt-pool dimensions.
Real-time dynamic laser-power modulation improves control of cooling rates.
Improved control of melt-pool dimensions and cooling rates produces finer microstructural features.
Improved control of melt-pool dimensions and cooling rates lowers defect density.
Combining moderate preheating with dynamic laser-power modulation produces a more homogeneous and refined microstructure.
Combining moderate preheating with dynamic laser-power modulation decreases porosity and residual stress.
The intervention will reduce deviation from target dimensional tolerances by an estimated 20–30% relative to constant-power LPBF without preheating.
The intervention will increase yield strength relative to constant-power LPBF without preheating.
The intervention will reduce susceptibility to crack initiation relative to constant-power LPBF without preheating.
The predicted benefits may not occur in alloys with very high thermal conductivity.
The predicted benefits may not occur in alloys that are sensitive to prolonged preheating.
